title: LEGO Icons Star Trek USS Enterprise Bridge reviewed: modular set scores 8/10
summary: Brick Fanatics has published its review of LEGO Icons 11385, the 1,701-piece modular USS Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set, praising its display options and minifigures but flagging fiddly instructions and heavy sticker use.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has reviewed LEGO Icons 11385 Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge, an 18+ set with 1,701 pieces (a nod to the ship's registration number). It's a modular playset recreating the original 1960s-style bridge, following on from last year's 10356 U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701-D.

The set is built around a C-shaped base with angled wall-mounted computer stations, plus separate modules for the captain's chair, helm console, viewscreen and turbolift. Reviewers compared its construction style to the 2016 LEGO Star Wars Carbon-Freezing Chamber set, sharing a similar grey, black and orange colour scheme.

The review awarded the set 8/10 overall, with strong marks for playability, value and minifigures (9/10 each), but a lower design score (7/10). Praised points included the unique modular design, multiple play/display configurations and near-perfect crew minifigures. Criticisms included unclear building instructions, an excessive number of stickers, and a suggestion that a transporter room element should have been offered as a gift-with-purchase instead.

## Why it matters
This is only the second LEGO Icons Star Trek set, so it's an important signal for how far LEGO Group is willing to expand this newer licensed theme. For fans of TV/film-based Icons builds and modular display sets, it's a useful early verdict before committing to the purchase.

title: New LEGO Batman minifigure reopens the Clone Trooper 'kama' debate
summary: The reveal of LEGO's newest Batmobile and its posable moulded Batman figure has fans asking again why Star Wars Clone Troopers like Captain Rex lost their fabric skirt pieces for printed legs.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The LEGO Group has officially revealed 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile, its fourth Batmobile set of 2026. It's a 2,269-piece build priced at £189.99, available to LEGO Insiders from 1 September before a wider release on 4 September. The set includes an exclusive Batman minifigure with a moulded cowl-and-cape piece, giving him a more solid, statue-like look inspired by Michael Keaton's film costume.

That design choice has fans revisiting an older complaint from the LEGO Star Wars side. Since 2023's 75367 Venator-Class Republic Attack Cruiser (a UCS set), the LEGO Group has moved away from fabric "kama" skirt pieces on Clone Troopers, including fan-favourite Captain Rex, in favour of printed detailing on the legs. According to comments previously given by LEGO Graphic Designer Madison O'Neil, this was done for consistency and play functionality, since fabric kamas can be tricky for children to fit and can stop minifigures sitting down.

Fans now point out that if a heavily moulded, hard-to-pose Batman piece is acceptable for a premium adult-focused set, the same logic arguably could have allowed fabric kamas to stay on similarly premium Star Wars sets like the Venator UCS.

## Why it matters
Minifigure accuracy versus play functionality is a long-running tension for LEGO designers, and this comparison highlights it clearly. For collectors and display builders, small design choices like this affect how faithfully a minifigure matches its on-screen source, and how it poses on a shelf.

## What to watch next
It's worth keeping an eye on whether fan pressure prompts any rethink on kama pieces in future adult-aimed Star Wars UCS sets, or whether the LEGO Group sticks with its printed-leg approach across the range.

title: LEGO DC's Batmobile habit: over half of sets this decade feature the car
summary: A new set breakdown shows just how Batmobile-heavy the LEGO DC theme has become, with 2026 confirmed as the most Batmobile-packed year yet.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Group has officially announced 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile, a 2,269-piece set based on the 1992 Tim Burton film, priced at £189.99. It's available to LEGO Insiders from 1 September, with a wider release on 4 September.

This is notable because it's the fourth Batmobile set of 2026 alone. Looking at the wider picture, analysis from Brick Fanatics shows that 21 of the 40 LEGO DC sets released since January 2020 have featured a Batmobile - that's 52.5% of the theme's entire output this decade.

2026 is currently the most Batmobile-heavy year yet, with four of six widely released LEGO DC sets (66.7%) including the vehicle. 2025 wasn't far behind at 60%. By contrast, 2020 and 2022 had the lowest share, at 40% each - though 2022 (the year of *The Batman* film) still saw every single DC set feature either a Batmobile or the Batcycle.

## Why it matters
For collectors and fans, this highlights a clear pattern in how LEGO DC sets are designed - vehicle variety can feel limited even as new versions keep arriving. If you're deciding whether to add another Batmobile to your shelf, or hoping for more non-vehicle DC sets, this data gives useful context on just how dominant the car has become in the range.

## What to watch next
With 76355 confirmed and already the fourth Batmobile of the year, it's worth watching whether LEGO Group diversifies into other DC vehicles or characters for future 2026 and 2027 releases, or continues leaning heavily on the Batmobile as a reliable seller.
